name: Read a numeral beyond 10 000
description: Student can read a natural number beyond 10 000 written as a numeral.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown 24 580, the student reads it as 'twenty-four thousand, five hundred and eighty'.
commonError: Student reads digit by digit, or ignores the thousands grouping.
checkpointTask: Show numerals beyond 10 000 with spaced thousands. Ask the student to read each aloud.

name: Write a numeral beyond 10 000
description: Student can write a numeral beyond 10 000 from its number name, using correct spacing.
exampleOfSuccess: Hearing 'thirty-two thousand and seven', the student writes 32 007.
commonError: Student leaves out the place-holding zeros, writing 327 for 'thirty-two thousand and seven'.
checkpointTask: Say several numbers beyond 10 000. Ask the student to write each numeral with correct spacing.

name: State the value of each digit
description: Student can state the place value of each digit in a number beyond 10 000.
exampleOfSuccess: In 47 130, the student says the 7 stands for 7 thousand.
commonError: Student names the digit but not its place value, or counts places from the wrong end.
checkpointTask: Point to digits in a 5-digit number. Ask the student the value of each.

name: Order numbers beyond 10 000
description: Student can order a set of numbers beyond 10 000 from smallest to largest.
commonError: Student orders by length of numeral or by leading digit only.
checkpointTask: Give five numbers beyond 10 000. Ask the student to order them.

name: Rename using place value
description: Student can rename a number across place values using materials or a place value chart.
exampleOfSuccess: The student shows 1 300 as 13 hundreds, moving materials on a place value model.
commonError: Student thinks renaming changes the total, or cannot regroup across a place.
checkpointTask: Pose a renaming task (how many hundreds in 1 300). Ask the student to show it.

name: Find one more across a boundary
description: Student can name the number that is one more than numbers ending in 9s, such as 99, 199, 1 009, 9 999.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked one more than 9 999, the student says 10 000.
commonError: Student cannot cross multiple boundaries at once, saying 9 9910 or similar.
checkpointTask: Ask one more than 99, 199, 1 009 and 9 999.

name: Recognise a unit fraction as an equal part
description: Student can recognise that a unit fraction such as 1/4 is one of a number of equal parts of a whole.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown a shape split into 4 equal parts, the student says one part is one quarter.
commonError: Student calls any one piece a quarter even when the parts are unequal.
checkpointTask: Show shapes split into equal and unequal parts. Ask the student which show quarters.

name: Name unit fractions
description: Student can name the unit fractions 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 and 1/10.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown a tenth of a strip, the student names it one tenth.
commonError: Student names by the number of pieces shaded rather than the size of the part.
checkpointTask: Show unit fractions of strips or shapes. Ask the student to name each.

name: Represent a fraction in different ways
description: Student can represent a unit fraction or its multiple in different ways, such as on a number line, area model or set.
exampleOfSuccess: The student shows 3/4 as shaded parts of a shape and as a point on a number line.
commonError: Student can show a fraction one way only, or mislabels the number line.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to show 3/4 in two different ways.

name: Show multiples of a unit fraction
description: Student can show multiples of a unit fraction, such as 2/5 or 3/4.
exampleOfSuccess: For 3/5, the student shades 3 of 5 equal parts.
commonError: Student shades the wrong number of parts, or makes the parts unequal.
checkpointTask: Name several fractions (2/4, 3/5, 7/10). Ask the student to show each.

name: Combine fractions to make a whole
description: Student can combine fractions with the same denominator to complete a whole.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 1/4 and 1/4 and 1/4 and 1/4 make one whole.
commonError: Student adds the denominators as well, giving 4/16 for four quarters.
checkpointTask: Pose 'how many quarters make a whole' and similar for fifths and tenths.

name: Connect fractions to sharing
description: Student can connect a sharing situation to a fraction.
exampleOfSuccess: Sharing 1 sandwich between 4 people, the student says each gets one quarter.
commonError: Student shares unequally, or does not name the share as a fraction.
checkpointTask: Pose equal-sharing situations. Ask the student what fraction each share is.

name: Add two- and three-digit numbers without regrouping
description: Student can add two- and three-digit numbers that do not require regrouping, using place value.
exampleOfSuccess: For 234 + 145, the student adds hundreds, tens and ones to get 379.
commonError: Student adds digits across columns incorrectly, or lines up the numbers wrongly.
checkpointTask: Pose additions with no regrouping. Ask the student to solve using place value.

name: Add with regrouping
description: Student can add two- and three-digit numbers that require regrouping a ten or hundred.
exampleOfSuccess: For 167 + 256, the student regroups ten ones and ten tens to get 423.
commonError: Student writes a two-digit number in a single column instead of regrouping.
checkpointTask: Pose additions needing regrouping. Ask the student to solve and explain the regrouping.

name: Subtract with regrouping
description: Student can subtract two- and three-digit numbers that require regrouping.
exampleOfSuccess: For 503 - 168, the student regroups to subtract and gets 335.
commonError: Student subtracts the smaller digit from the larger in each column regardless of position.
checkpointTask: Pose subtractions needing regrouping. Ask the student to solve and explain it.

name: Partition to add or subtract
description: Student can partition numbers by place value to add or subtract.
exampleOfSuccess: For 320 + 450, the student adds 300+400 and 20+50 to get 770.
commonError: Student partitions inconsistently or loses a part when recombining.
checkpointTask: Pose additions and subtractions. Ask the student to solve by partitioning.

name: Use the inverse to check
description: Student can use the inverse relationship to check an addition or subtraction.
exampleOfSuccess: After working 423 - 168 = 255, the student checks with 255 + 168 = 423.
commonError: Student repeats the same operation to check rather than using the inverse.
checkpointTask: After the student solves a subtraction, ask them to check it using addition.

name: Use a constant-difference strategy
description: Student can adjust both numbers by the same amount to make a subtraction easier.
exampleOfSuccess: For 403 - 198, the student adds 2 to both to get 405 - 200 = 205.
commonError: Student adjusts only one number, changing the answer.
checkpointTask: Pose subtractions near a round number. Ask the student to make them easier and solve.

name: Represent multiplication as equal groups
description: Student can represent a multiplication as a number of equal groups.
exampleOfSuccess: For 4 groups of 3, the student makes 4 groups of 3 counters and says 12.
commonError: Student makes groups of unequal size, or counts groups instead of objects.
checkpointTask: Pose multiplications as equal groups. Ask the student to model and find the total.

name: Use an array for multiplication
description: Student can represent a multiplication as an array of rows and columns.
exampleOfSuccess: For 3 x 5, the student makes 3 rows of 5 and says 15.
commonError: Student miscounts the array, or confuses rows and columns.
checkpointTask: Pose multiplications. Ask the student to build an array and find the total.

name: Write a multiplication number sentence
description: Student can write a multiplication number sentence for a situation.
exampleOfSuccess: For 6 bags of 4 apples, the student writes 6 x 4 = 24.
commonError: Student writes an addition sentence, or the wrong factors.
checkpointTask: Pose grouping situations. Ask the student to write a multiplication sentence.

name: Divide by sharing
description: Student can solve a division by sharing into equal groups.
exampleOfSuccess: Sharing 18 between 3, the student finds 6 each.
commonError: Student leaves a remainder unshared when it should be shared, or shares unevenly.
checkpointTask: Pose sharing problems. Ask the student to solve and write what each gets.

name: Divide by grouping
description: Student can solve a division by making equal groups of a set size.
exampleOfSuccess: For how many teams of 4 from 20, the student finds 5 teams.
commonError: Student answers how many in each group instead of how many groups.
checkpointTask: Pose grouping problems. Ask the student how many groups.

name: Connect multiplication and division
description: Student can use the link between multiplication and division to solve a problem.
exampleOfSuccess: Knowing 4 x 6 = 24, the student says 24 divided by 6 = 4.
commonError: Student treats multiplication and division as unrelated.
checkpointTask: Give a multiplication fact. Ask the student to state a related division fact.

name: Estimate the size of a collection
description: Student can estimate the number of objects in a collection.
exampleOfSuccess: Glancing at a jar, the student estimates about 50 counters.
commonError: Student guesses wildly with no reference, or insists on counting exactly.
checkpointTask: Show collections. Ask the student to estimate how many before counting.

name: Estimate using a known amount
description: Student can use a known quantity as a benchmark to estimate a larger one.
exampleOfSuccess: Knowing one handful is about 10, the student estimates 5 handfuls is about 50.
commonError: Student does not use the benchmark, or multiplies incorrectly.
checkpointTask: Give a benchmark amount. Ask the student to estimate a larger collection using it.

name: Choose what to round to
description: Student can choose a sensible place value to estimate to for a situation.
exampleOfSuccess: Estimating a crowd, the student rounds to the nearest hundred.
commonError: Student rounds to a place value that is too precise or too coarse.
checkpointTask: Pose situations. Ask the student what they would round to and why.

name: Check if an answer is reasonable
description: Student can use estimation to judge whether a calculation is reasonable.
exampleOfSuccess: For 298 + 305, the student estimates about 600 and sees that 603 is reasonable.
commonError: Student accepts an unreasonable answer without checking, or cannot estimate to compare.
checkpointTask: Give a calculation and an answer. Ask the student to estimate and say if it is reasonable.

name: Choose the operation for a problem
description: Student can choose whether a practical problem needs addition, subtraction, multiplication or division.
exampleOfSuccess: For 'share 24 among 4', the student chooses division.
commonError: Student picks the operation by the biggest number rather than the situation.
checkpointTask: Pose four practical problems. Ask the student which operation each needs.

name: Model an additive problem with a bar model
description: Student can model an additive problem using a bar model or diagram.
exampleOfSuccess: For a part-part-whole problem, the student draws a bar with the parts and whole.
commonError: Student draws a model that does not match the quantities in the problem.
checkpointTask: Pose an additive problem. Ask the student to model it with a bar model.

name: Model a multiplicative problem
description: Student can model a practical multiplication or division problem with materials or a diagram.
exampleOfSuccess: For 'how many wheels on 6 cars', the student models 6 groups of 4.
commonError: Student adds the numbers instead of modelling groups.
checkpointTask: Pose a multiplicative problem. Ask the student to model and solve it.

name: Solve a financial problem
description: Student can model and solve a practical money problem.
exampleOfSuccess: For 'buy 3 items at $4 each', the student finds $12.
commonError: Student ignores the dollar context or chooses the wrong operation.
checkpointTask: Pose a money problem. Ask the student to solve it and answer in dollars.

name: Interpret the solution in context
description: Student can interpret and communicate a solution in terms of the situation.
exampleOfSuccess: After finding 24, the student says '24 apples, that is enough for the class'.
commonError: Student gives a bare number without connecting it back to the problem.
checkpointTask: After the student solves a problem, ask what the answer means for the situation.

name: Follow an algorithm
description: Student can follow an algorithm of steps and decisions to investigate numbers.
exampleOfSuccess: Following a double-it algorithm from 1, the student generates 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.
commonError: Student skips a step or ignores a decision point.
checkpointTask: Give a step-by-step number algorithm. Ask the student to follow it and record the result.

name: Use an algorithm with a decision
description: Student can follow an algorithm that includes a decision, such as testing a multiple.
exampleOfSuccess: Using an 'is it a multiple of 5' rule, the student sorts numbers correctly.
commonError: Student applies the rule inconsistently or ignores the decision branch.
checkpointTask: Give an algorithm with a yes/no decision. Ask the student to apply it to several numbers.

name: Create an algorithm
description: Student can create a simple algorithm of steps for a classmate to follow.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes steps to generate multiples of 3.
commonError: Student writes steps that are unclear or miss a step, so they cannot be followed.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to write steps a classmate could follow to make a number pattern.

name: Describe the emerging pattern
description: Student can describe a pattern that emerges from following an algorithm.
exampleOfSuccess: After doubling repeatedly, the student says the numbers keep getting twice as big.
commonError: Student lists the numbers but does not describe the pattern or rule.
checkpointTask: After running a number algorithm, ask the student to describe the pattern they see.
